Rosy Anand
--Revisionist
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand and Another
--Respondents
Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Rajat Mittal, learned counsel
for the revisionist.
Ms. Pushpa Bhatt, learned
Additional Advocate General assisted by
Mr. Prabhat Kandpal, learned A.G.A.
assisted by Mr. Nikhil Bisht, learned
Brief Holder for the State of
Uttarakhand.
Ms. Priya Mewari, learned counsel
for respondent no. 2.
2. The present Criminal Revision has
been preferred against the judgment and
order dated 04.06.2026, passed by the
learned IInd Additional Sessions Judge,
Rishikesh, District Dehradun in
Criminal Appeal No. 33 of 2025, whereby
the appeal preferred by the revisionist
was dismissed and the judgment and
order dated 30.04.2025, passed by the
learned Additional Civil Judge
(J.D.)/Judicial Magistrate, Rishikesh,
District Dehradun in Criminal Complaint
Case No. 1225 of 2016, was affirmed. By
the said judgment, the revisionist was
convicted for the offence punishable
under Section 138 of the Negotiable
Instruments Act, 1881, and was
sentenced to undergo rigorous
imprisonment for a period of six months
along with a fine of ₹3,40,000/-, out of
which ₹5,000/- was directed to be
deposited in the State Treasury and the
remaining amount of ₹3,35,000/- was

UKHC010139222026
2026:UHC:7001
directed to be paid to the
complainant/respondent no. 2 as
compensation. The revisionist was
further directed to undergo simple
imprisonment for a period of thirty days
in default of payment of fine.
3. Learned counsel for the parties
submit that, after the judgment was
passed in the appeal, the parties have
amicably settled their dispute.
4. A joint compounding application,
duly signed by the learned counsel for
the revisionist as well as the learned
counsel for respondent no. 2, has been
filed before this Court. In the said
application, it has been averred that the
dispute had arisen in respect of the
cheque in question and that the
revisionist has now paid the entire
cheque amount to the complainant
/respondent no. 2, which fact has been
admitted by both the parties.
Consequently, they have prayed that the
offence, being compoundable in nature,
be permitted to be compounded in
accordance with law.
5. Today, the revisionist and
respondent no. 2 are present before this
Court through video conferencing and
have been duly identified by their
respective learned counsel.
6. Both the parties have submitted
that the entire cheque amount has been
paid to respondent no. 2 and that
respondent no. 2 has no grievance
against the revisionist. They have further
stated that, in view of the amicable
settlement arrived at between them, they
wish to bring the present proceedings to
an end.
7. Having regard to the amicable
settlement arrived at between the parties
and considering that the offence under
Section 138 of the Negotiable
Instruments Act, 1881, is compoundable

UKHC010139222026
2026:UHC:7001
this Court is of the considered view that
no useful purpose would be served by
allowing the impugned judgments and
orders to stand. Accordingly, the present
Criminal Revision is allowed. The
judgment and order dated 04.06.2026,
passed by the learned IInd Additional
Sessions Judge, Rishikesh, District
Dehradun in Criminal Appeal No. 33 of
2025, as well as the judgment and order
dated 30.04.2025, passed by the learned
Additional Civil Judge (J.D.)/Judicial
Magistrate, Rishikesh, District Dehradun
in Criminal Complaint Case No. 1225 of
2016, are hereby quashed and set aside.
8. Consequently, the compounding
application stands allowed and is,
accordingly, disposed of.
(Alok Mahra, J.)
 07-08-2026
